title: Package architecture
text: Pandoc/Quarto render .qmd original.docx reference-doc. alone enough carry original’s styles, header, footer, section properties — ’s native Pandoc behavior, custom code involved. post-render hook runs automatically (thin shim _extensions/officequarto/scripts/writeback.R calls package’s exported oq_writeback()): resolves path reference-doc via quarto inspect, works copy freshly rendered .docx temporary directory, transfers docProps/core.xml (subject, keywords, description, category) docProps/custom.xml (freely defined custom properties) original — metadata Pandoc otherwise replaces fresh, empty values rendering. result overwrites .docx produced Quarto place; original (reference-doc) left untouched. officequarto.keep-rendered: true, plain, unpatched Pandoc output additionally saved beforehand <name>.quarto-rendered.docx (analogous Quarto’s keep-md — handy debugging, see Pandoc produced without hook). also strips style definitions word/styles.xml Pandoc added aren’t present reference-doc (see vignette("options")’s “Style pruning” section).

what: Style-mapping: map body text onto your own Word style
title: Configuring officequarto
text: Pandoc renders body paragraphs using styles defined reference-doc, , fixed style names (depending context, e.g. Normal, FirstParagraph, Compact) rather , possibly differently named style template (e.g. Fließtext German corporate template). officequarto.styles.body lets customize — analogous {officedown}’s mapstyles/Normal mapping: provide style name visible Word UI (internal style ID) — hook resolves word/styles.xml reference-doc. Body paragraphs detected via allowlist known Pandoc body roles (Normal, FirstParagraph, Compact, BodyText/ Body Text). configured style name doesn’t exist reference-doc, hook aborts list available paragraph styles instead silently ignoring misconfiguration. allowlist never matches footnote/endnote text, even though otherwise reachable style-mapping mechanisms — see Footnotes endnotes .
code: format:   docx:     reference-doc: original.docx     officequarto:       styles:         body: "Fließtext ACME"   # real style name from original.docx

title: Configuring officequarto
text: officequarto.lists mirrors officequarto.styles.body list paragraphs — analogous {officedown}’s ol.style/ul.style: three fields optional independent; roles aren’t configured stay Pandoc’s default styles. List paragraphs detected via presence <w:numPr> (style name, since Pandoc uses style regardless list type). List type distinguished via word/numbering.xml (w:numFmt): bullet → list-bullet; lowerLetter/upperLetter (markdown ./. markers) → list-letter; anything else (decimal, roman numerals, …) → list-number.
code: format:   docx:     officequarto:       lists:         list-bullet: "Aufzählung ACME"         list-number: "Nummerierung ACME"         list-letter: "Buchstabierung ACME"    # a/b/c or A/B/C lists - officequarto-only, no officedown equivalent

title: Configuring officequarto
text: list-bullet/list-number/list-letter also accepts array style names instead single value — one style per nesting level, index 0 = top level: nesting level deeper array clamps deepest configured entry — convention Word’s built-styles use (List Bullet/List Bullet 2/List Bullet 3: nothing beyond level 3 either, deeper indents just keep reusing ). plain scalar still works exactly (style every level) — officequarto-extension, {officedown} per-nesting-level equivalent ol.style/ul.style.
code: officequarto:   lists:     list-bullet: ["Aufzählung ACME", "Aufzählung ACME 2", "Aufzählung ACME 3"]

title: Configuring officequarto

See Option reference full canonical-name/alias table (filled incrementally {officedown} option groups ported).

title: Configuring officequarto
text: officequarto.tables lets control every table rendered document formatted — analogous {officedown}’s tables option, ported first group broader {officedown}-option port (see Option reference): three fields independently optional (per-field opt-, like officequarto.styles/ officequarto.lists) — unset field left exactly Pandoc rendered , ’s forced fallback officedown’s defaults. style resolved reference-doc’s table styles (paragraph styles), fail-loud lookup body/list-bullet/etc. layout/width written directly onto every table’s w:tblPr (w:tblLayout/w:tblW), inserted OOXML-schema order alongside whatever w:tblPr children Pandoc already produced. officedown’s tab.lp option (bookdown cross-reference label-prefix) deliberately ported — ’s authoring-syntax concept equivalent Quarto already resolved cross-references hook ever runs. need change visible “Table”/“Figure” caption prefix text, use Quarto’s native crossref.tbl-title/crossref.fig-title _quarto.yml instead — officequarto option needed .

title: Configuring officequarto
text: officequarto.tables.conditional controls Word’s “Table Style Options” checkboxes (Header Row, Total Row, First/Last Column, Banded Rows/Columns) — variant table style’s conditional formatting gets applied table: field independently optional, style/layout/width. band-rows/band-columns officequarto’s , positively-phrased names officedown’s no_hband/no_vband — officedown aliases (tables_conditional_no_hband/tables_conditional_no_vband) still work carry opposite polarity (no_hband: false means thing band-rows: true); hook resolves negates correctly, including conflict warning set contradictory values.
code: format:   docx:     officequarto:       tables:         conditional:           first-row: true       # highlight header row           first-column: false           last-row: false           last-column: false           band-rows: true       # alternating row shading           band-columns: false

what: Table captions: style, prefix, separator, bold
title: Configuring officequarto
text: officequarto.tables.caption controls table captions formatted — analogous {officedown}’s tables.caption: field independently optional. style remaps Pandoc’s caption paragraph role way code-block remaps SourceCode — tables specifically, TableCaption plain markdown caption (: caption, crossref ID) ImageCaption role shared figures Quarto crossref-managed one ({#tbl-xyz}); officequarto detects structure applies touches paragraphs structurally identified table captions, figure ones — see dev/spike-notes.md (Spike L) empirical trail. prefix/separator/number-bold inherently fragile everything else officequarto, ’s worth understanding : Quarto’s docx table captions currently render static, already-baked-text (e.g. "Table 1: caption" single text run), real Word field — ’s live number hook . officequarto rewrites text fact locating sequential table number printed (counting captioned tables document order, way Quarto numbers ) splicing configured prefix/separator around . one part Pandoc’s generated text approach doesn’t try predict shape auto-generated prefix — can vary crossref.tbl-title/title-delim settings, additionally reshaped Pandoc’s smart-typography conversion (e.g. configured -- becomes real “–” character, non-breaking space number) — rather reconstructing string config, officequarto anchors number (immune typographic conversion) find split point. caption doesn’t match expected “prefix + number + separator + text” shape, ’s left untouched rather guessed . Note applies Quarto crossref-numbered caption first place — plain markdown caption ({#tbl-xyz}) never auto-numbered Quarto , ’s generated prefix split ; style still applies , prefix/separator/number-bold make sense numbered captions. officedown’s tnd/tns (per-section numbering depth, e.g. "2-1") ported — Quarto numbers tables globally, per heading section, ’s existing per-section counter key ; replicating mean officequarto tracking heading boundaries maintaining numbering scheme, substantially larger feature direct precedent elsewhere project.

"                       # text before the number (officedown: pre)           separator: " -- "                     # text between number and caption (officedown: sep)           number-bold: true                     # bold the "prefix + number" portion only

what: Figure captions: style, prefix, separator, bold
title: Configuring officequarto

title: officequarto 0.1.0
text: Initial development version. yet CRAN. Converted project proper R package (officequarto), Quarto extension powers bundled inside inst/_extensions/. R package now required runtime dependency: extension’s post-render hook thin shim calls package’s exported oq_writeback(). Added oq_create_project() scaffold new officequarto project R (modeled usethis::create_project()), copying bundled extension, optional reference document, _quarto.yml listing every officequarto option default value. Paragraph style-mapping body text lists (officequarto.styles, officequarto.lists), including per-nesting-level list styles officedown-compatible option aliases. Table options: style/layout/width, conditional formatting, captions (officequarto.tables). Figure options: style/alignment captions (officequarto.plots). Caption position control (caption.) tables figures. Free-form style remapping (officequarto.style-map), including footnote/endnote paragraph styling. Page size/margins (officequarto.page). Cross-reference text control (officequarto.crossref.numbered) live, renumbering Word SEQ/REF fields (officequarto.crossref.auto-number). Added automatic style pruning: styles Pandoc adds absent reference-doc removed rendered .docx, opt-escape hatch code-block styling (officequarto.pandoc-styles.code-block). Added vignette("architecture") vignette("options"), pkgdown site published main.
